flawed_step: Contracting the triangle produces a bridgeless cubic graph, but such a graph need not be 3-edge-colourable.
counterexample: Start with the Petersen graph having outer cycle a0-a1-a2-a3-a4-a0, spokes ai-bi, and inner cycle b0-b2-b4-b1-b3-b0. Replace a0 by a triangle xyz, replacing a0a1, a0a4, a0b0 by xa1, ya4, zb0. Thus the edges are xy,yz,zx, xa1,ya4,zb0; a1a2,a2a3,a3a4; aibi for i=1,2,3,4; and b0b2,b2b4,b4b1,b1b3,b3b0. This is finite, simple, cubic, and bridgeless: the triangle edges lie on a cycle, and every other edge lies on a cycle lifted from the bridgeless Petersen graph. If it had a 3-edge-colouring, the three triangle edges would receive all three colours. Consequently xa1, ya4, and zb0 would also have three distinct colours. Contracting xyz to a0 would therefore give a 3-edge-colouring of the Petersen graph. But the Petersen graph is not 3-edge-colourable: every perfect matching has either all five spokes or exactly one spoke, and its complement consists of two 5-cycles; whereas in a cubic 3-edge-colouring the complement of any colour class must alternate between the other two colours and hence consist only of even cycles. Contradiction.
assessment_summary: Expanding a vertex of the Petersen graph into a triangle gives an explicit bridgeless cubic graph containing a triangle but admitting no 3-edge-colouring.
